salmon: Rich in omega-3 fatty acids (EPA and DHA) that reduce vascular inflammation, help lower triglycerides, and support cardiovascular health.
oats: High in soluble fiber (beta-glucans) which helps lower LDL cholesterol and reduces postprandial glucose spikes.
spinach: Excellent source of potassium and magnesium, both essential for blood pressure regulation and cardiac rhythm stability.
broccoli: Contains sulforaphane and other compounds that support vascular endothelial function and have anti-inflammatory properties.
blueberries: Rich in anthocyanins with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties that may improve vascular function.
almonds: Contain monounsaturated fats that help lower LDL cholesterol while maintaining HDL cholesterol. Also rich in vitamin E.
dark_leafy_greens: High in nitrates that support nitric oxide production, improving vascular function and lowering blood pressure.
beans_legumes: Excellent source of soluble fiber and plant-based protein, helping with cholesterol control and sustained energy.
sweet_potato: Rich in potassium and beta-carotene with a lower glycemic index, supporting blood glucose control.
turkey: Lean protein source low in saturated fat, supporting muscle maintenance without increasing cardiovascular risk.
chicken_breast: High-quality lean protein with minimal saturated fat content, ideal for heart-healthy diets.
olive_oil: Contains monounsaturated fats and polyphenols with anti-inflammatory and cardioprotective properties.
greek_yogurt: High in protein and probiotics, supports gut health and provides beneficial micronutrients.
whole_wheat_bread: Complex carbohydrate with sustained nutrient absorption, preventing rapid blood glucose elevation.
brown_rice: Good source of B vitamins and minerals with a lower glycemic index than white rice.
tomatoes: Rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that may reduce cardiovascular disease risk.
garlic: Contains allicin which has mild antiplatelet and antihypertensive properties.
walnuts: Source of alpha-linolenic acid (plant omega-3), supporting cardiovascular health and reducing inflammation.
avocado: Contains potassium for blood pressure control and monounsaturated fats for cholesterol management.
carrots: Rich in beta-carotene and fiber, supporting cardiovascular health and glucose control.
bell_peppers: High in vitamin C and antioxidants, supporting immune function and vascular health.
lentils: Excellent source of plant-based protein and soluble fiber for cholesterol and glucose management.
quinoa: Complete protein containing all essential amino acids, with a lower glycemic impact.
fish: Excellent source of high-quality protein and omega-3 fatty acids without excessive saturated fat.
low_fat_milk: Provides calcium and vitamin D for bone health without excess saturated fat.
apple: Rich in soluble fiber (pectin) that helps lower LDL cholesterol and supports satiety.
orange: High in vitamin C and fiber, supporting immune function and cardiovascular health.
strawberries: Rich in anthocyanins and vitamin C with anti-inflammatory properties.
unsalted_nuts: Provide healthy fats, minerals, and satiety without excess sodium.
hummus: Plant-based protein and fiber from chickpeas with healthy fat from olive oil.
barley: Contains beta-glucans similar to oats, supporting cholesterol reduction and glucose control.
beets: Rich in dietary nitrates that support vasodilation and blood pressure control.
mushrooms: Contain compounds that support immune function and have anti-inflammatory properties.
cinnamon: May have modest effects on blood glucose control and has anti-inflammatory properties.
ginger: Has anti-inflammatory properties and may support digestive health.
turmeric: Contains curcumin with powerful anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties.
green_tea: Rich in catechins, antioxidants that support cardiovascular health and metabolic function.
low_sodium_broth: Provides flavor without excessive sodium, supporting DASH and other sodium-restricted protocols.
herbs_spices: Provide flavor without sodium, supporting medication adherence by making food more palatable.
white_fish: Lean protein source with minimal saturated fat, ideal for various medical diet protocols.
lean_beef: Provides iron, B12, and other micronutrients, but should be consumed in controlled portions.
tofu: Plant-based complete protein source suitable for those seeking alternatives to animal protein.
chickpeas: Excellent source of plant-based protein and fiber for sustained energy and cholesterol management.
kale: Very high in vitamins K, C, and contains compounds with potential anti-inflammatory properties.
cantaloupe: Rich in potassium for those not on potassium-restricted diets, and in vitamin C.
pear: Good source of soluble fiber with a relatively lower glycemic index.
cherries: Contain anthocyanins and may have anti-inflammatory properties.
asparagus: Low in calories, rich in folate and other micronutrients, supports overall health.
cauliflower: Low glycemic impact, rich in vitamin C and sulforaphane compounds.
zucchini: Low in calories and carbohydrates, supportive for various medical diet protocols.
cottage_cheese: Good source of protein with lower sodium options available.
egg_white: Pure protein source without yolk cholesterol, suitable for heart-healthy diets.
grapeseed_oil: Source of polyphenols, though should be avoided with certain medications.
sesame_seeds: Rich in calcium, magnesium, and lignans with anti-inflammatory properties.
flaxseeds: Source of alpha-linolenic acid and lignans with potential cardiovascular benefits.
chia_seeds: Complete protein with omega-3 fatty acids and soluble fiber.
honey: Natural sweetener with antioxidant properties, though calories should be counted.
vinegar: May have modest beneficial effects on glucose control and satiety.
lemon: High in vitamin C and compounds that may enhance iron absorption.
papaya: Rich in enzymes supporting digestion and in vitamins A and C.
mango: Source of vitamins A, C, and fiber, though portion control needed for glucose management.
